newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary forint up vs dlr, unaffected by rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Hungary forint up vs dlr, unaffected by rate cuts.

text.p: The Hungarian forint firmed against the dollar, remained steady versus the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) currency basket and was unaffected by recent central bank rate cuts, dealers said on Monday.
The forint tracked the dollar/mark all day, remaining pinned to the NBH resistance level (bid), and closed at 185.20/25 to the dollar, up from midday's 185.53/58 and the opening's 185.75.

Dealers said the NBH's deposit rate cuts last Friday and repo rate reductions a week earlier did not affect the market as forint interest rates still remained attractive compared with foreign currencies.
The NBH reduced the six-month and twelve-month deposit rates by 50 basis points on Friday, following 50 basis point cuts in four of its five repo rates one week before.
"There is still an (interest rate) differential on which investors can have profits," said BNP-Dresdner Bank's Mihaly Donka. "And also the (monthly forint) devaluation (rate) is likely to be cut."
Analysts said earlier the government and the central bank were likely to cut the monthly 1.1 percent devaluation rate by 0.1 percentage point for the second half of the year.
(The NBH's floating intervention band is 4.5 percent wide. The forint floats against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.)
